thread:
Alex: quick poll — my roommate decided right before standup that today is vacuum day. my laptop mic is picking everything up. anyone tried using plants or other cheap stuff as a sound dampener? pics appreciated :grimacing:
Maria: I used a tall potted ficus behind my desk once, helped a bit for reflections. rugs + curtains are the real MVPs. also try moving the mic off the desk (shock mounts help). :house_with_garden:
Devon: condenser laptop mics are brutal for that. cheap trick: flip to the laptop's lowest gain and use push-to-talk, or get a dynamic USB mic (SHURE SM58-style USBs are forgiving).
Samira: also noise suppression in calls is fine — enable it in Meet/Zoom. if you want a DIY hack: drape a blanket over two chairs and sit under the tent while on calls. looks silly but lowers background by a lot. :towel:
Luke: posted my setup a while back — small IKEA shoe box, lined with felt, propped behind my mic as a tiny absorber. works surprisingly well for near-field. here's the ascii of the "blanket tent" idea:
```
chair  <- blanket -> chair
   \_______desk_______/
       mic inside
```
Alex: lol love the tent. does anyone have a quick parts list for a mini shield? thinking of building one tonight.
Maria: cardboard, old hoodie/felt, hot glue, and some velcro strips. cut a semicircle to wrap behind the mic. took me 15 mins and it muted the fan hum.
Devon: ops-bot just pinged that infra is doing a brief reimage at 11:30 — maybe try to avoid heavy calls then? @ops-bot any ETA?
ops-bot: reminder: scheduled infra maintenance at 11:30–11:50 UTC. some homebrew CI agents might reconnect, nothing user-facing expected. :gear:
Samira: hey Alex — if you want, I can drop by (virtually) with my camera and help place the blanket/plant for max effect. cheap hacks are my specialty. :seedling:
Alex: thanks everyone! trying blanket tent + cardboard shield tonight, will post pics if it turns into a Pinterest disaster. :camera_with_flash:
